Q: How to properly compress images for recycler view A:

When you take the image, instead of just creating the image, create a thumbnail (a smaller version of the image) as well. Store the location of both the main image and the thumbnail in your db, each in its own column. In the recycler's adapter, display the thumbnail instead of the full image. This will take much less memory and time (as you aren't resampling on display). When you want to display a big version of the image, use the full sized one.

Q: Does the C++ standard guarantee that `std::vector<T>::data()` returns the pointer returned by the allocator? A:

Short answer: No guarantee.

Every implementation will do so though. vector implementations are allowed (and encouraged) to allocate for extra objects at the end of the vector, there is no reason why they couldn't also allocate extra objects at the front (if for some reason that standard library implementation wanted a more efficient erase from the front and insert to the front).

You should just use CxxVector<T> to be able to deallocate from Rust

Q: How to get a less than and greater than range in an IFS Statement using AND A:

In addition to the @AvdTorre's answer the IFS function returns the result after the first match, so you need to set the conditions in reverse order (and you don't have to recheck what has already been checked).

=IFS(L4>Settings!$G$6,Settings!$F$6,L4>=Settings!$G$5,Settings!$F$5,L4<Settings!$H$4,Settings!$F$4)

Q: Why is void | MyType<void> an acceptable return type under no-invalid-void-type? A:

My question is "what is the design philosophy and / or technical reason why the linter accepts the union void | SomeType<void> when any other union with void is disallowed?" I believe there has to be a single objective answer to this question. In an ideal world, the answer would come from whomever designed and implemented this linter rule. I am not interested in a discussion about the usefulness / validity of the rule itself, linting practices, the quality of the example code. Does that clarify my intent? If yes, how should I rephrase the question to better express what I am looking for?

Q: Using XSLT3.0 in Saxon-JS 2, how can one configure the processor so that it accepts codepoints-to-string(8)? A:

I don't think it is possible to use XML 1.1 with SaxonJS in the browser as for XML parsing it relies on the browser's underlying XML parser where I don't know of a browser that supports XML 1.1.

It is however, in the meantime, possible, to run Saxon HE Java in the browser, with a tool called CheerpJ which basically compiles the Java class files to web assembly/JavaScript and that way runs the Java code in the browser. Probably not what you are looking for at this point but I thought I mention it as it allows using XML 1.1, example at this link.

Q: What does the "system" version mean in node version manager? A:

If anyone comes across this Question:

System indicates the manually installed node version.

Check the manually (non-nvm) installed node version and may remove it.
